fieldFixes.summary: The UN Human Rights Council's resolution 28/16, 'The right to privacy in the digital age', adopted without a vote on 26 March 2015, decided to appoint for three years a special rapporteur on the right to privacy, tasked among other things with gathering information on international and national frameworks and practices. It was the first UN mandate dedicated to privacy. The first mandate-holder, Joseph Cannataci of Malta, was selected in July 2015, and his mandate began on 1 August 2015.

fieldFixes.summary: The Standing Committee of China's National People's Congress adopted the Cybersecurity Law on 7 November 2016, and it took effect on 1 June 2017. The law firm DLA Piper describes it as the first national-level law to address both cybersecurity and data-privacy protection. Its Article 37 required operators of critical information infrastructure to store within China the personal information and important data they collect and generate in their operations there, and to pass a security assessment before any necessary transfer abroad.

issues: False claim: 'Uruguay was the first non-European state to approve it, in 2021.' Mauritius signed and deposited its instrument of ratification of CETS 223 on 4 September 2020, becoming 'the 6th State after Bulgaria, Croatia, Lithuania, Poland and Serbia as well as the first country in Africa' to ratify (Data Protection Office of Mauritius communiqué, FOUND). All five earlier ratifiers are European, so Mauritius, not Uruguay, was the first state outside Europe. Uruguay's parliament approved the protocol only in April 2021. The Ferrere headline repeats the error, probably carried over from Uruguay being the first non-European state to accede to the original Convention 108 (2013), which the article's first paragraph mentions.
The Ferrere quote is verbatim and still supports 'signed in Strasbourg in October 2018', so it is kept for that fact only. Its note is corrected.

displayDate 'October 2018' is correct. The protocol opened for signature on 10 October 2018, but the exact day could not be read by script (coe.int and rm.coe.int return 403), so the month-level date is kept. Adoption by the Committee of Ministers on 18 May 2018 is now sourced verbatim from the Council of Europe's own Convention 108+ booklet (June 2018), hosted by the European Parliament.

Checked and correct: Slovakia deposited its ratification on 15 June 2023 as the 25th state (FOUND on the Slovak DPA page). The significance line's 'only candidate for a binding global privacy treaty' matches the Mauritius communiqué's 'the only existing legally binding international treaty with global relevance in this field' (FOUND). Strasbourg coordinates are right.

fieldFixes.summary: The protocol modernising Convention 108 (CETS No. 223), known as Convention 108+, was adopted by the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers on 18 May 2018 and opened for signature in Strasbourg in October 2018, updating the 1981 treaty for the GDPR era. Ratification has been slow: Slovakia's, deposited on 15 June 2023, was the 25th. The first state outside Europe to ratify was Mauritius, which deposited its ratification on 4 September 2020 as the sixth state overall.

The exact opening date (10 October 2018) could not be read on coe.int, which blocks scripts.

issues: Wrong date. Parliament passed the Personal Data Protection Bill on Wednesday 9 March 2022, per News 1st, 09-03-2022: 'The Personal Data Protection Bill was passed in Parliament with amendments on Wednesday (9).' (FOUND) 19 March 2022 is the date the Speaker certified it, which is when the bill became law; the Act's own header reads '[Certified on 19th of March, 2022]' (FOUND). The DLA Piper source conflates the two dates.

The title states 'South Asia's first dedicated data-protection law' as fact. That is the Data Protection Authority's own description. Nepal's Individual Privacy Act, 2018 (2075), which includes personal-information provisions, predates it (listed by DLA Piper as Nepal's data-protection law, FOUND). So 'first' should be attributed, as the summary already does, and not asserted in the title. The title is reworded. The record id still contains 'first' but is not user-facing.

fieldFixes.title: Sri Lanka passes a dedicated personal-data protection law
fieldFixes.summary: Sri Lanka's Parliament passed the Personal Data Protection Bill with amendments on 9 March 2022, and the Speaker certified it on 19 March as the Personal Data Protection Act No. 9 of 2022. The country's Data Protection Authority describes it as the first independent personal-data legislation in South Asia; Nepal's broader Individual Privacy Act of 2018 also covers personal information. The Act was amended by Act No. 22 of 2025.
fieldFixes.sources[1].note: Law-firm global guide (secondary). Its date is wrong: 19 March 2022 is the date the Speaker certified the Act, not the date Parliament passed the bill (9 March 2022, per News 1st). The quote is verbatim but is kept only for the Act's name and number.
